sourceCoverage.rule: Every authoritative effect, zone, ground item, backing sheet, encounter-resource directory, present initiative tracker, active reservation, and pending encounter-item decision appears exactly once in temporary cleanup.
sourceCoverage.ambiguity: A stable source identity resolving to more than one authoritative object fails closed.
sourceCoverage.extraOrMissing: Foreign, duplicate, and omitted cleanup source identities fail before a write preview becomes applicable.

owningContracts.combatStages: The existing item combat-stage encounter lifecycle handler emits one typed all-stage reset over exact sheet-backed placements.
owningContracts.temporaryEffects: Turn, round, and encounter durations expire through the existing encounter-end effect lifecycle; Scene, campaign-time, explicit-dismissal, until-triggered, and permanent durations remain unless an exact reviewed cleanup behavior says otherwise.
owningContracts.resources: Encounter-end clears structured turn resources and encounter history through their existing reducers.
owningContracts.zones: Zone durations follow the same encounter-boundary duration distinction; each preserve, expiry, or transform remains source-specific.
owningContracts.groundItems: Map-owned ground items persist by default and leave only through an explicit expire behavior or exact provider-bound transform.
owningContracts.initiative: A declared initiative cleanup clears encounter-scoped placement scores and resets the normalized tracker to no active placement at round one.
owningContracts.sceneState: Active Scene identity, Scene move usage, Scene temporary HP, Scene effects, Scene form changes, campaign-time effects, HP, injuries, persistent conditions, inventories, equipment, and advancement remain untouched.
owningContracts.reservations: Reservations are derived from pending item operations. Any active reservation remains a blocker and is never released by cleanup as a substitute for resolving or abandoning its owning operation.

transformations.identityRule: The transformed value retains the exact source identity and passes its strict owning parser.
transformations.authorityRule: Every transform names one exact provider authority; a decision-selected transform must match the authority pinned by that accepted option.
transformations.forbidden: Generic JSON patches, cross-kind replacement, identity changes, and text-derived mechanics are rejected.

fields: reset, expire, preserve, transform, exclude, or pending action
preview.explainability: Every changed or preserved temporary source has one deterministic action row; open choices and blockers remain explicit.
preview.privacy: The complete preview is server-private. Later projections expose only audience-safe labels, action, changed state, and blocker summaries.

writePlan.map: All map-owned cleanup composes into at most one next map revision with stable-JSON SHA-256 before and after evidence.
writePlan.sheets: Each changed sheet receives one revision with exact previous and next hashes; HP, injuries, conditions, and unrelated permanent fields are retained.
writePlan.determinism: The encounter-end event identity derives from settlement identity, map identity, and exact map revision; no browser clock, random client value, or array-order accident owns cleanup.
writePlan.staleRule: Application rechecks the complete authority hash, exact map and sheet revisions, before hashes, after hashes, and monotonic next revisions.
writePlan.atomicRule: Open decisions, active reservations, pending encounter items, denied authorization, stale state, incomplete coverage, or invalid transforms expose no applicable writes. P8-080 persists all resulting writes with the settlement transaction.

replay.planning: The same settlement and exact authority produce byte-equivalent write plans and result codes.
replay.terminal: Committing, completed, cancelled, applied, or receipted cleanup cannot be replanned as new work.
replay.retry: A stale plan must be rebuilt from a fresh complete read; it is never rebased by source label or replayed as a new command.
